root_cause.text: The Bluetooth L2CAP Enhanced Credit Based reassembly function l2cap_ecred_data_rcv() failed to validate that the skb contained the 2-byte SDU length field before calling get_unaligned_le16(skb->data), causing an out-of-bounds read on short PDUs.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that l2cap_ecred_data_rcv() read the SDU length from skb->data “without first verifying that skb contains at least L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE (2) bytes,” and the patch adds `if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE)) { err = -EINVAL; goto failed; }` immediately before `get_unaligned_le16(skb->data)`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Bluetooth L2CAP Enhanced Credit Based reassembly function l2cap_ecred_data_rcv() failed to validate that the skb contained the 2-byte SDU length field before calling get_unaligned_le16(skb->data), causing an out-of-bounds read on short PDUs.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that l2cap_ecred_data_rcv() read the SDU length from skb->data “without first verifying that skb contains at least L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE (2) bytes,” and the patch adds `if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE)) { err = -EINVAL; goto failed; }` immediately before `get_unaligned_le16(skb->data)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length-availability check before reading the SDU header in `l2cap_ecred_data_rcv()` to reject malformed short skbs safely.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added at the start of the `!chan->sdu` block in `l2cap_ecred_data_rcv()` to call `pskb_may_pull(skb, L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE)` before reading the SDU length; if the check fails, `err` is set to `-EINVAL` and execution jumps to the `failed` label.
intent_record.how: This ensures the skb contains at least enough linear data for the 2-byte SDU length field before `get_unaligned_le16(skb->data)` and `skb_pull()` access it, preventing invalid packet parsing and potential out-of-bounds access on short or malformed packets.

grouping_result.intent: Add a length-availability check before reading the SDU header in `l2cap_ecred_data_rcv()` to reject malformed short skbs safely.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by checking that the skb contains the 2-byte SDU length field before reading it in l2cap_ecred_data_rcv(), preventing the out-of-bounds read on short PDUs.

candidates.rationale: This reads the 2-byte SDU length from skb->data without first verifying that the skb contains at least L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE bytes, directly causing the out-of-bounds read on short PDUs.

This consumes 2 bytes from the skb assuming the SDU length field is present; while secondary to the root cause, it relies on the same missing length validation and is part of the unsafe handling of short skbs.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement reads a 2-byte SDU length from skb->data without first verifying that the skb contains at least L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE bytes. On malformed short PDUs, it can perform an out-of-bounds read, which is the stated root cause.

This statement advances the skb by 2 bytes under the same unchecked assumption that the SDU length field is present. It is part of the vulnerable sequence that mishandles short skbs after the missing bounds validation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the exact start-of-SDU parsing logic. In the newly added path `if (!chan->sdu)`, the code immediately does `sdu_len = get_unaligned_le16(skb->data);` and then `skb_pull(skb, L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE);` with no prior check that `skb->len >= L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE` (2 bytes). The only earlier size check is `if (chan->imtu < skb->len)`, which limits maximum PDU size but does not ensure a minimum length of 2. Therefore a short skb can reach `get_unaligned_le16(skb->data)` and trigger the out-of-bounds read described in the root cause. Since the required length validation before reading the SDU length field is absent, the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet in this function.
